title: Luma Uni-1.1 Guide: Features, Price and Prompts
summary: Luma Uni-1.1 guide: what Luma's reasoning image model does, what it costs in Flick, and real tests of likeness, posters, manga, storyboards and Max.
body_markdown:
### What is Luma Uni-1.1?


Luma Uni-1.1 is Luma AI's image generation and editing model. Luma describes it as a reasoning model that thinks through a prompt and draws in one network, and it reads up to nine reference images.


### How much does Luma Uni-1.1 cost?


In Flick, Luma Uni-1.1 costs 10 credits an image at Standard quality and 20 at Max, plus 1 credit for each reference image connected.


### Is Luma Uni-1.1 free?


Luma Uni-1.1 runs on Flick's Free plan, and each image uses credits. A new Flick account gets 100 credits, enough for several Luma Uni-1.1 images at Standard.


### What is the difference between Uni-1.1 and Uni-1.1 Max?


Max is Uni-1.1's higher quality setting, at double the price. In our premiere test, Max drew sharper sign lettering and followed more of the prompt's details, such as the Art Deco front and the rain.


### How many reference images does Luma Uni-1.1 take?


Up to 9. In Flick you connect them to the image node and @-mention each one in the prompt, and each adds 1 credit to the price.


### Can Luma Uni-1.1 write Japanese or Arabic text?


Yes, in our tests. It wrote three Japanese speech balloons and an Arabic film title, "الطريق الطويل", correctly, and Luma says it renders Chinese, Japanese and Arabic natively.


### What aspect ratios does Luma Uni-1.1 support in Flick?


Five: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 3:2 and 2:3. A default 16:9 image measured 2672 × 1504 in our tests, and a 2:3 poster 1632 × 2464.
